audit.whatIsWrong: 'Searing Charge needs terrain, so fight him away from walls and he literally cannot answer your lockdown.' He brings his own terrain.
audit.why: Riot's text for Volcanic Rupture: 'Ornn slams the ground, sending out a fissure dealing damage and slowing enemies hit. After a small delay, a magma pillar forms at the end location.' Searing Charge then 'creates a shockwave... if Ornn collides with terrain while charging'. The pillar is the terrain. Standing in open lane does not disarm the combo — he casts Q at 800 range, waits the delay, and charges his own pillar. That single sentence is the difference between a safe all-in and walking into a knockup.
audit.corrected: spikes[1].text, mid, whys[2] and whys[4] now say he creates the terrain himself, and the timing cue is the pillar's delay rather than the map's walls.
sources: champ-data/_kits/ornn.json (Q Volcanic Rupture, E Searing Charge)

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Repudiation's shield eats his Bellows Breath Brittle setup' and 'brace Repudiation... so the shield eats the knockup'. A shield does neither.
audit.why: Riot's text: Repudiation gives a shield, braces, then slams, and 'if she blocked any non-minion damage while bracing herself, this ability will deal increased damage'. It absorbs damage. Brittle is a debuff applied by Bellows Breath's final gout, and the Searing Charge shockwave is a knockup — neither is damage, so neither is absorbed. What Repudiation genuinely does here is get paid for the damage that arrives alongside them.
audit.corrected: spikes[2].text, mid and whys[5] now say the brace is paid by his damage, and stop promising it cancels Brittle or the knockup.
sources: champ-data/_kits/ornn.json (W Bellows Breath, E Searing Charge)

audit.whatIsWrong: 'A Maxim-empowered auto' appears in spikes[0].text, wants.you[1], early and whys[1]. Ambessa has no ability called Maxim.
audit.why: Her empowered attack comes from Drakehound's Step: 'Entering an attack or movement command while casting an ability will cause Ambessa to dash a short distance once the ability is cast, granting her next attack bonus range, damage, and attack speed, and refunding energy.' This is the same class of invented name as 'Ares of Blaze' for Brand.
audit.corrected: All four now name Drakehound's Step.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'His double-knockup Call of the Forge God' is stated twice, and Living Forge is mentioned only as 'he self-itemizes'.
audit.why: Riot's text: the elemental's first pass leaves enemies 'damage[d], slowed and made Brittle' — no knockup. Only the recast, where Ornn charges into it and redirects it, knocks up. Calling it a double knockup makes the first pass sound unsurvivable and the second sound routine, which is backwards. Living Forge is also more than a shop: he 'gains an additional bonus Armor and Magic Resist from all sources', so every resistance item he buys is worth more than it says on the tooltip — the real reason an all-physical Ambessa cannot out-scale him.
audit.corrected: spikes[3].text, late and whys[6] now split the two passes and state what Living Forge actually amplifies.
sources: champ-data/_kits/ornn.json (P Living Forge, R Call of the Forge God)

audit.whatIsWrong: Ornn is called 'one of the slowest, most immobile bodies you will lane into' and 'a dashless tank' twice, and no cooldown appears anywhere in the matchup.
audit.why: Searing Charge is a charge on 14/13.5/13/12.5/12 at 450 range, and Call of the Forge God's recast is another one. He is slow, not immobile. The numbers the entry needs: Volcanic Rupture 9s at rank 1 from 800, Bellows Breath 12s, Searing Charge 14s, and his ultimate at 140s against Public Execution's 130s — the only ultimate in this slice that comes back slower than hers.
audit.corrected: Numbers in spikes[0].text, mid, whys[2], whys[3], breakdown.cooldowns and dosFull[0].d; 'dashless' replaced with the charge and its cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: mid credits 'Public Execution's armor-pen passive' with chewing through his plating, and early tells the player to hit 'the doubled outer edge of your Q'.
audit.why: Public Execution's text is a 1250-range blink to the farthest enemy champion in a line, a suppression on arrival, then a slam that damages and stuns — no passive, no penetration. Cunning Sweep's text gives 'bonus damage to enemies hit by the blades', with no edge sweetspot and no multiplier. Both invented, and against a champion who amplifies his own resistances the fake penetration is the more damaging one.
audit.corrected: mid now leans on the suppression, early says the blades.
sources: champ-data/_kits/ambessa.json (Q Cunning Sweep, R Public Execution)

audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart gives Ornn four stages, Skill three and Ambessa none, while the prose calls the mid game 'your takeover' and the recorded win rate is 53.89% to Ambessa over 488 games.
audit.why: Chart, prose and data all disagree. I could not propose a fix: swapping a side means writing 'Ambessa' (7 characters) where 'Ornn' (4) stands, a 75% change that the applier's length band rejects outright. The same blocker is documented in the completed nasus/ambessa mirror.
audit.corrected: Left every side and rating untouched and raised it as a question. The whys I did rewrite were kept factual about the abilities rather than reworded to claim a winner either way.

edits.before: Ornn is one of the slowest, most immobile bodies you will lane into, and he has no sustain to grind you back. At level 1 you both have one ability, so trade your Q cone over the minions and just don't stand against a wall when his Volcanic Rupture pillar lands. Once you have Q-into-Sundering-Slam plus a Maxim-empowered auto at 2-3, you out-trade his Q poke flat — dash-weave in, hit the doubled outer edge of your Q, then step out before his Searing Charge can pop you off a wall. His one real punish is pillar-into-E for the Brittle knockup; bait that cooldown, then commit.

Brace Repudiation into his damage and the slam comes out bigger; it will not stop the Brittle or the knockup, so time the exit.

Build your lead before that matters, and respect that one Brittle shatter amplifies his whole team's CC landing on you in a 5v5.

notes: The finding that changes how the lane is played: the entry told the player that fighting away from walls disarms Searing Charge, but Volcanic Rupture leaves a magma pillar after a short delay and that pillar is the terrain the charge collides with. Open lane is not safe; the pillar is the cue. Two more mechanical corrections: Repudiation is a shield, so it cannot 'eat' the Brittle debuff or the Searing Charge knockup as the entry twice promised — it only gets paid for damage blocked; and Call of the Forge God's first pass slows and applies Brittle while only the recast knocks up, so 'double-knockup' was wrong. Living Forge's real value here is that it adds armour and MR from ALL sources, which is why an all-physical kit cannot out-scale him. Also removed: the invented ability 'Maxim' for her empowered auto (it is Drakehound's Step), 'the doubled outer edge' of Cunning Sweep, and Public Execution's non-existent armour-pen passive. UNVERIFIED: the existing claim that Bellows Breath grants damage reduction. Riot's description mentions only the advance, the fire and the Brittle on the final gout, so I did not restate it — I wrote the Brittle instead. LEVEL CHART: Ornn holds four stages and Ambessa none, against a 53.89% Ambessa win rate over 488 games and prose that calls the mid game her takeover. I could not propose the fix — 'Ornn' to 'Ambessa' is a 75% length change and the applier rejects it.
